AC-1 A locally-authenticated administrator holding the required role binding is PERMITTED for a role-gated action with an empty actor_authz_state table (test).
AC-2 A local session without the binding is DENIED with a reason, never unevaluated and never permitted; a directory-authenticated session behaves exactly as before (tests).
AC-3 The audit row distinguishes a local permit from a directory permit.
AC-4 An empty credential list in the add-device dialog offers creation, creating one selects it and enables submit, and a role refusal renders as a sentence (frontend tests).
AC-5 Eleven-module build, service, persistence, architecture and frontend tests, privacy gate and contract_authority_status green.

baseline.authority: docs/design/PO_DECISION_RECORD_2026_09_14J_NEXUSADMIN_IS_THE_PRODUCTS_ROOT_IDENTITY.md -- FROZEN 2026-09-14: RT-1 the product has exactly one root identity, the nexusadmin the first boot seeds, holding every authority above any directory-derived one; RT-2 the evaluator answers PERMITTED for it for every action whatever the required role token and whatever the directory state, and neither an unevaluated stale group set nor an unbound role token applies to it; RT-3 it is recognised by its SEEDED IDENTITY ID, never by its name, and nothing a client sends can make a session claim it; RT-4 it cannot be disabled or locked out; RT-5 root is not invisibility -- every action is audited and the decision row records that the permit came from the ROOT AUTHORITY, distinct from a binding permit and a directory permit, so an auditor can separate allowed-because-root from allowed-because-entitled; RT-6 root outranks the directory. Its section 2: every other identity is authorized exactly as C3 specifies, unchanged. docs/design/PO_DECISION_RECORD_2026_09_13G_LOCAL_IDENTITY_ADMINISTRATION_AND_CLI_PARITY.md -- FROZEN: LIA-1..LIA-6, local identity administration is reachable from the UI and the CLI, an operator administers local identities and their role bindings without a directory. docs/design/UI2_0_C3_IDENTITY_SESSIONS_RBAC_CONTRACT.md (FROZEN) -- the authorization model, its decision outcomes (PERMITTED, DENIED, AUTHZ_NOT_EVALUATED, NO_APPLICABLE_AUTHORITY), its reason codes and the rule that a stale group set is never silently downgraded to a permit. This movement adds a second authority for locally-authenticated sessions; it removes none of C3's guarantees and keeps every refusal auditable. PO ASSISTANT DECISION 2026-09-14, on the Product Owner's own objection: a local-only install must not require a directory to authorize anything, and a dialog that needs a credential must let the operator create one rather than refuse.
baseline.test_baseline: Run ./ui2/gradlew -p ui2 build -x :integration-tests:test, :service:test, :persistence:test, :architecture-tests:test and npm --prefix ui2/frontend test first; record counts.
baseline.what_exists: The defect, observed live today: an authz_decisions row reads action_id credential_list, outcome AUTHZ_NOT_EVALUATED, reason_code actor_group_set_stale, authority ui2_ldap, and the actor_authz_state table was empty, so every action with a required role token was refused for the local administrator while the open ones (device_read, notifications_read) returned NO_APPLICABLE_AUTHORITY and worked. RbacEvaluator (ui2/service/.../security/RbacEvaluator.java) is the single decision point: it looks up the required role token, finds the active bindings for it, then reads actorAuthzStateRepository.find(actorFingerprint) and returns Decision.notEvaluatedStale() when that is absent or not fresh; only afterwards does it compare the actor's group references with each binding's decrypted group reference. LocalRoleTokenResolver (same package) already resolves a local identity's roles by decrypting each active binding's group reference and comparing it with the local identity id -- the local bindings store the identity id AS the group reference. The two are never connected. The Product Owner assistant has seeded one actor_authz_state row by hand so the operator could continue; that is a one-off unblock, not the fix, and the fix must make it unnecessary. Frontend: ui2/frontend/src/shell/AddDeviceDialog.tsx renders a Credential select whose options come from listCredentials and disables its submit when the list is empty; ui2/frontend/src/screens/CredentialsPanel.tsx is the existing create/replace/delete surface for the encrypted credential store.

invariants: The root identity is recognised by its seeded id, never by a name or anything a client can set.
A root permit is always audited and always distinguishable from an entitled permit.
A local-only install never needs a directory to authorize anything.
No refusal is silently downgraded to a permit.
The operator never sees a bare machine code as an explanation.
Secrets are typed once and never returned.

report.objective: Make a local-only install usable and correct in three connected ways. First, implement record 14J: the seeded root identity is permitted for every action, recognised by its seeded id, and its permits are audited under their own authority. Second, authorize ordinary locally-authenticated identities from their own role bindings instead of demanding a directory-resolved group set, which today refuses every role-gated action. Third, stop the add-device dialog dead-ending when no credential exists: let the operator create one there, stored encrypted, and continue.
output_contract: A local-only install where the administrator's own roles authorize them, and a dialog that lets them create the credential it needs.

recommended_reasoning.reason: One decision point to extend with an existing resolver, plus a dialog affordance over existing endpoints.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Every change names the clause it implements (13G LIA-n, C3 section n).

Do NOT use './ui2/gradlew -p ui2 build' without '-x :integration-tests:test'. Do not run the full Python pytest suite. Eleven Gradle subprojects. No migration unless genuinely required; if one is, it is additive and sets the audit context before any row it writes.
No credential, secret or identity value reaches a log line, an exception message or an HTTP response.
A refusal the operator can see must be a sentence in the interface; the machine-readable code stays in the payload and the audit row.
Mechanical mismatches between this packet and the code are settled against the code and named in the SESSION_CLOSE; a RELAY_QUESTION is for a decision in conflict.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the PR or code comments.
Commit early and often. SESSION_CLOSE names how a local session is recognised, the new authority value, the dialog affordance, and test counts before and after.
risks: Matching the root identity by name, which would let a renamed or re-created identity inherit root.
Permitting root without writing the audit row, which trades a lockout for an invisible superuser.
Permitting on the local path without checking the binding, which would open every role-gated action.
Deciding a session is local from something the client can set.
Leaving the hand-seeded actor_authz_state row as the thing that makes the tests pass.
Duplicating the binding-decryption loop instead of reusing the resolver.

in: Root identity (14J RT-1..RT-6): RbacEvaluator permits the seeded root identity unconditionally, before any binding or group-set check; the identity is matched by the id first boot recorded (read the first-boot seeding code for where that id lives and resolve it without trusting anything the client sends -- if no durable marker exists, add one in the seeding path and say so); the decision row records a root authority distinct from the binding and directory authorities; the root identity cannot be disabled and its own access-restoring actions are never blocked by the four-eyes rule. Tests: root is permitted for an action whose role token has no binding at all and with an empty actor_authz_state; the audit row names the root authority; a second identity sharing only its NAME is not root.

Authorization for locally-authenticated sessions: RbacEvaluator gains a local authority path -- when the session's actor is a local identity, its roles come from the local role bindings (reuse LocalRoleTokenResolver; do not write a second decryption loop), and a permit records that authority and the binding id exactly as the directory path does. The directory path is unchanged for directory-authenticated sessions, and a local session with no binding for the required token is DENIED with its own reason code, never PERMITTED and never left unevaluated. Decide and state how the evaluator knows a session is local (the session record, the actor fingerprint's shape, or an explicit field -- read the login path and pick the one that cannot be spoofed), and say which in the SESSION_CLOSE.
The seeded actor_authz_state row must stop being necessary: a test proves a local administrator with a security_admin binding is PERMITTED for credential_list with an empty actor_authz_state table.
Every outcome stays auditable: the authz_decisions row for a local permit names the local authority, not the directory one, so the two can be told apart afterwards.

Inline credential creation: when the add-device dialog's credential list is empty, it offers to create one instead of refusing -- a create affordance in the dialog itself that posts to the existing credential endpoints, with the same fields the credentials panel uses (the secret is typed once, stored encrypted, never returned), and on success selects the new credential and continues. When the operator lacks the role to create one, the dialog says so plainly instead of showing an empty control with a refusal code. The refusal code must never be the whole message the operator sees: map it to a sentence.

Tests: service tests for the local permit, the local deny and the directory path unchanged; a test that an empty actor_authz_state does not block a local administrator; frontend tests that an empty credential list offers creation, that creating one selects it and enables submit, and that a role refusal renders a sentence rather than a code.

entries.subject: Local deny reason code conflicts with C3 invariant
entries.text: WORKER.md requires a local session without its required binding to be DENIED with its own reason code, while the same dispatch prohibits changing C3 reason codes. The current RbacEvaluator declares C3's closed vocabulary as actor_not_in_required_group, role_token_unbound, and actor_group_set_stale. Please decide whether local denial must reuse actor_not_in_required_group with a distinct local authority, or whether the FROZEN contract authorizes a new local-specific reason code.

entries.subject: Local deny reuses actor_not_in_required_group; the authority field carries the difference
entries.text: Good question, and the answer needs no new code. Reuse the existing C3 reason code actor_not_in_required_group for a local denial. It is literally accurate: a local role binding stores the local identity id AS its group reference, so an identity without that binding is not in the group the binding names. C3's closed reason vocabulary therefore stays exactly as it is -- no new value, no amendment. What distinguishes the two paths is the AUTHORITY recorded on the decision row, not the reason: a directory decision records the directory authority, a local decision records a local authority, and a root permit records the root authority per 14J RT-5. Those three values are what an auditor reads to tell the paths apart. So: add the authority value, reuse the reason code, and keep role_token_unbound and actor_group_set_stale meaning exactly what they mean today for the directory path. Nothing else in the packet changes.
